walkthroughs.body_html: Africa has 54 countries and over 1.4 billion people. It crosses the Equator, with tropical zones, deserts and grasslands.
North: Sahara desert. South of it: the Sahel. Around the Equator: rainforest. Further south: savannah and even temperate Mediterranean climates.
The Nile is the world's longest river. Mount Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest peak. The Great Rift Valley stretches thousands of km!

mcqs.q: What does a 'large scale' map mean?
options: A large-scale map covers a small area in high detail (e.g. 1:25,000 OS map of one town); a small-scale map covers a large area in less detail (e.g. 1:1,000,000 world atlas).
A large-scale map shows a large area.
Large scale means the map is physically big.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a choropleth and an isoline map?
options: Choropleth and isoline maps are the same thing.
Choropleth maps are for showing churches and isoline maps are for showing roads.
Large scale means the map is physically big.
Choropleths use coloured/shaded areas to show data values per region (e.g. population density by county); isoline maps use lines connecting points of equal value (e.g. contours, isobars).

mcqs.q: Why is the urban heat island effect strongest at night?
options: Urban heat islands only happen in summer.
Urban heat islands are strongest at midday because cities are sunniest then.
Concrete and brick released their stored daytime heat slowly into the night air, while rural areas cool rapidly through radiative loss — widening the urban-rural temperature gap after sunset.
